Baltimore bills as a city, not a county

Baltimore has been an independent city since 1851. Baltimore County surrounds it, but the two are separate governments, so no county bill sits on top of the city's. The 2020 census counted 585,708 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 569,997. Housing is mostly rowhouses, many with brick or formstone fronts, and many blocks fall in historic districts, which can limit exterior work. Ask before you assume a quick cosmetic fix is allowed.

One city bill carries the city rate and the state rate together, and the office that collects it also runs the annual tax sale. A tax balance here deserves attention early.

Rates and how a bill is figured

The city rate is $2.248 per $100 of assessed value, and the state adds $0.112 per $100 on the same bill, which the city forwards to the state. The combined rate is $2.360 per $100. The state assessments office, SDAT, sets each parcel's value, and the city applies its rate to that figure. The budget office's tax-rate page shows $2.248 for fiscal 2027.

Tax or creditRate or limit
City real property rate$2.248 per $100 of assessed value
State rate on the city bill$0.112 per $100
Combined$2.360 per $100
Homestead credit cap, from July 1, 20264% a year on a principal residence
City transfer tax1.5% of the cash consideration
Recordation tax$5.00 per $500 of consideration paid

Transfer and recordation taxes yield less on sales over $1 million, and part of each goes to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund. Your sales contract decides who pays at closing.

The 2026 reassessment and the homestead cap

Baltimore was in Maryland's Group 2 reassessment, and residential full cash value rose 13.4% between January 1, 2023 and January 1, 2026. Increases phase in evenly over three years, and decreases apply in full for the 2026 tax year. If you live in the house and have applied for the homestead credit, the 4% cap means a big jump in market value does not become a big jump in taxable value right away.

If you inherited a house or moved out years ago, check whether the credit is still attached. It needs a principal residence, so a rental or empty house can lose the cap and see the taxable value catch up faster.

Due dates, interest and the tax sale

Bills are mailed July 1 and are due on receipt, with a half-percent discount if paid by July 31. After October 1, unpaid tax accrues 1% interest plus a 1% monthly penalty. Owner-occupied homes and small businesses with taxes under $100,000 can pay in two equal installments, with a small fee added to the second. A pending appeal does not excuse a late payment, but a successful one produces a refund with interest.

A property becomes eligible for the annual tax sale when it is behind by at least $750 on an owner-occupied residence or $250 on a non-owner-occupied one.

  • First week of February: Final Bill and Legal Notice mailed to the address in land records.
  • First week of April: second letter.
  • May: the online tax sale.
  • First week of July: post-sale informational letter.

You can stop a sale by redeeming, which means paying the winning bidder all claims, interest and costs. A Tax Sale Deferral Program run through Finance and Housing and Community Development can keep a property out of the sale for a year.

Other city charges that become liens

Unpaid annual registration fees on non-owner-occupied property are a lien and can go to tax sale. They surprise many sellers, since the fees are small and easy to miss on a rental or an inherited vacant house.

  • 1- and 2-family dwellings: $30 per dwelling unit.
  • Multifamily dwellings: $35 per dwelling unit or $25 per rooming unit.
  • Vacant residential structures: $100 per structure plus $30 per dwelling unit.
  • Vacant lots: $25 per lot.

Owners of registered vacant buildings must keep them clean and secure until they are razed or rehabilitated, and the city bills the owner if it does the work first. A 2024 state law also lets the City Council set a special tax rate on abandoned properties. Call the city to learn whether a rate applies to your parcel.

Weather, flooding and older rowhouses

Elevation ranges from sea level at the harbor to about 480 feet in the northwest. Lower blocks near the water see more flooding, while hillside neighborhoods deal with drainage and old foundations. Buyers and inspectors look hard at basements, rear additions and roofs on rowhouses after a wet year, so gather any repair records before you list.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What closing looks like with a city balance

At settlement the title company totals the city payoff, any registration fees and the transfer and recordation taxes your contract assigns to you. The payoff must be good through the closing date, which is why a figure requested weeks earlier may be too low once interest or penalties keep accruing. Ask for an updated number a few days before you sign.

Vacant houses draw extra attention. The housing department reported 13,411 vacant building notices as of mid-2024, 863 of them on city-owned property, so a boarded-up house you own may already be on a list. Keep it clean and secure, and resolve any registration charges before the sale so they do not delay the title work.

If the house has been in the family for years and the paperwork is a mess, tell the title company at the start. Sorting out who is the owner of record can take longer than paying the bill.

First steps when taxes are due

Find out what you owe and whether the property is marked for the May sale. The collections call center is 410-396-3000, and assessment questions and credits go to the state office at 410-767-8250.

  1. Pull the current bill on the city payment site and note any balance from earlier years.
  2. Check for registration or other city charges on the account.
  3. Ask for a payoff figure good through your expected closing date.
  4. Tell the title company early so the payoff is built into the settlement statement.

If money is tight, a payment plan or the deferral program may buy time. When the house also needs work and the balance keeps growing, selling as is for cash can clear the lien from the proceeds at closing. Call or text us with the address and we will tell you what we can offer.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Baltimore City property tax rate?

The city rate is $2.248 per $100 of assessed value, and the state adds $0.112 per $100 on the same bill. That is $2.360 combined, before any credits.

Does Baltimore property tax jump when my house is reassessed?

Not all at once for most owners. Increases phase in over three years, and a principal residence with the homestead credit is capped at 4% a year from July 1, 2026.

How much unpaid tax puts a Baltimore house into the tax sale?

A property becomes eligible once it is delinquent by at least $750 for an owner-occupied residence or $250 for other property. The sale is held online each May after notices in February and April.

Can I sell a Baltimore house that is already in the tax sale process?

Usually yes, but timing matters. Owners can stop a sale by redeeming, so ask the collections office for a payoff figure and tell your title company right away.

What are the Baltimore transfer and recordation taxes?

The city transfer tax is 1.5% of the cash consideration, and the recordation tax is $5.00 per $500 of consideration. Who pays each is set in the contract.

Where is the city of Frederick, Maryland?

Frederick is the seat of Frederick County, about 46 miles west of Baltimore, 50 miles north and slightly west of Washington, D.C., and 24 miles southeast of Hagerstown. It sits at 341 feet of elevation and covers 24.56 square miles, almost all of it land.

Daniel Dulany laid out the town by 1745, and it became the county seat when Frederick County was formed in 1748. Schifferstadt, built in 1756, is probably the oldest surviving house in the city. Frederick was a stop on the Great Wagon Road and the National Road, a rail and canal hub in the 1830s, and the site of the 1864 Battle of Monocacy.

The city counted 78,171 people in 2020, and the 2025 estimate listed by Wikipedia is 92,059.

What is the layout of Frederick, and where are the older neighborhoods?

Frederick has a dense, walkable historic core surrounded by newer growth, and the core is where most of the preservation rules apply. Market, Patrick and East Streets carry more than 200 retailers, restaurants and antique shops in the Frederick Historic District, and downtown has about 600 businesses and organizations.

  • West Patrick Street follows the former National Road, now U.S. 40.
  • Monocacy Boulevard is a circular road that supports the core.
  • Culler Lake is a man-made lake downtown, and the church spires give the city its Clustered Spires nickname.
  • First Saturday draws about 11,000 people on average to downtown each month.

How do roads and transit shape the Frederick housing market?

Several major roads meet in Frederick: I-70, I-270, U.S. 15 and U.S. 340 meet here. I-70 runs east-west toward Baltimore and Hagerstown, I-270 runs southeast toward Washington, and U.S. 15 runs north toward Gettysburg.

ConnectionWhat it does
I-70East-west link to Baltimore and Hagerstown
I-270Spur toward Washington, D.C.
U.S. 15North-south toward Gettysburg, Pennsylvania
MARC commuter railRuns to Washington on former B&O lines
Express bus 991Goes to the Shady Grove Metro station
Frederick Municipal Airport (FDK)General aviation

Local TransIT buses and Greyhound also serve the city.

Who are the major employers in and around Frederick?

Fort Detrick is the largest employer in the Frederick area, with 10,827 employees in the 2025 figures reported by Wikipedia, and the county school board is next at 7,433. The list below shows the main public and institutional employers.

  • Frederick Health: 3,360
  • Frederick County Government: 2,810
  • Leidos Biomedical Research: 2,370
  • Frederick Community College: 1,369
  • City government: 977

Riverside Research Park, on the east side, hosts the National Cancer Institute's Frederick National Laboratory. Hood College and Frederick Community College are the city's higher education campuses, and Mount St. Mary's University has a campus in Frederick County.

What is the weather in Frederick, and what does it mean for a house?

Frederick has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and generally cool winters. The mean daily high is about 88.6 degrees in July and 43.1 degrees in January.

Average annual precipitation is 43.52 inches, and average snowfall is 16.5 inches. The state record high of 109 degrees was set in Frederick on July 10, 1936.

Flooding has a local history. The Carroll Creek flood control project began in the late 1970s to reduce flood risk to downtown from the 100-year floodplain. Its first phase, costing nearly $11 million, runs from Court Street to just past Carroll Street. The Carroll Creek Overlay District in the city code sets design standards for new construction and rehabilitation near the creek. The park along it includes brick paths, water features, pedestrian bridges and a 350-seat amphitheater, and Wikipedia reports more than $150 million in private investment underway or planned nearby, covering office, retail, residential and parking development.

What property tax rate applies inside the city of Frederick?

A house inside the city of Frederick had a combined real property rate of 1.7382 per $100 of assessed value in the fiscal 2025 state table, made of a county rate and a city rate. The table is published by the Department of Legislative Services from SDAT data.

Piece of the rate (fiscal 2025)Per $100 of assessed value
County rate in the city1.0077
Municipal rate0.7305
Combined1.7382
Unincorporated Frederick County, for comparison1.1100

The county's Treasury page says each municipality levies its own district tax for services like street maintenance, trash removal and police, and that homestead credit caps vary by municipality from 0 percent to 10 percent.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What dates and appeal steps apply to a Frederick city owner?

Frederick County Treasury lists annual bills and the first installment as due September 30, with the second installment December 31, and interest of 1 percent per month starts October 1. Payments in July earn a 1 percent discount and August payments a one-half percent discount.

Assessments come from SDAT, which values property about every three years. An owner can appeal to the Supervisor of Assessments within 45 days of the notice date, to the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board within 30 days after that decision, and to the Maryland Tax Court within 30 days of the board's order. The SDAT office for the county is reached at 301-815-5350.

The county also lists a Senior Tax Credit of 20 percent of net county real property taxes for owners 65 or older who meet income limits, and a Homestead Tax Credit that limits yearly increases on a principal residence.

What historic district and code rules affect a Frederick seller?

In the city of Frederick, exterior work on a designated site or a property in a Historic Preservation Overlay district needs a certificate of approval from the Historic Preservation Commission. The commission reviews exterior features only and does not consider interior layout.

  • Changes do not have to be visible from the street to need review. Routine maintenance and landscaping with no material effect are exempt.
  • The commission has 45 days to act on a complete application, and silence means approval unless the applicant agrees to more time.
  • A certificate expires after three years without a building or zoning permit, with one six-month extension available.
  • Decisions can be challenged in the Circuit Court for Frederick County within 30 days.

Properties outside the overlay can still face demolition review when a plan removes more than 25 percent of floor area, changes significant roof lines or moves the structure.

For rental condition, the county says complaints about properties inside the city go to city inspectors at 301-600-3825.

Frequently asked questions

What is the property tax rate in Frederick, MD?

The fiscal 2025 state table shows 1.7382 per $100 of assessed value inside the city, made up of a 1.0077 county rate and a 0.7305 municipal rate. Rates are reset each year, so check the current notice.

When is Frederick property tax due?

September 30 for annual bills and the first installment, and December 31 for the second installment. Interest starts October 1 at 1 percent per month, and a 1 percent discount applies to July payments.

Who do I call about my Frederick property tax?

Call the Frederick County Treasury at 301-600-1111 for billing, and SDAT at 301-815-5350 for the assessed value. The Treasury is at 30 North Market Street, open 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays.

Does the Frederick Historic Preservation Commission review a house sale?

No, a sale itself does not require approval. Exterior work on a designated or overlay property does, and the commission has 45 days to act on a complete application.

Can I sell a Frederick house with back taxes?

Yes, unpaid tax can be paid from the closing proceeds by the title company. Ask the Treasury for a lien certificate or tax status report to see the exact amount before you set the closing date.
